threads.title: US-Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz
threads.current_state: The US launched a 'heavy wave' of new strikes on Iran; Iranian state media reports at least three civilians killed. Hours later, Iran struck Jordan and Kuwait, killing a worker at a Chinese-owned building in northern Kuwait. Trump said it is now 'our turn' to hit Iran hard. This is the first round of this cycle with confirmed civilian deaths directly attached to it.
threads.why_it_matters: Oil and rate risk both run through this - a direct input to Alex's CRE and markets picture, and now a story measured in reported deaths, not just oil-price basis points.

timeline.summary: First tracked: nine nights of US strikes, oil up about 20% this month, 10-day ceasefire being mediated.
10-day ceasefire formally proposed; US strikes continue, Iran calls it full-scale war, Brent tops $91, war cost estimated at $37.5B.
By Wednesday, strikes reach an eleventh consecutive night; Brent pushes past $92, reviving inflation concern.
Ceasefire proposal remains unadopted; Brent closes at $94.13, a five-week high; Strait transits fall to 25 ships from a peak of 49.
13th consecutive night of strikes; Iran hits Kuwait and the Houthis strike two Saudi tankers; Brent crosses $100 for the first time since May.
US carries out no new strikes overnight for the first time since the ceasefire collapsed; Brent eases to about $96.80.
Iran-aligned Houthi rebels fire dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities in Jizan and Yanbu.
The pause holds through the weekend into Monday with no new strikes reported; Brent tumbles toward the mid-$80s.
Trump and Netanyahu meet at the White House for the first time since the war began, calling the talks positive and productive; Brent eases further.
Iran says it struck US bases in Jordan and other Gulf locations overnight; Trump vows to hit back hard and repeats a bridge-bombing threat; Brent jumps back above $90.

The US launches a 'heavy wave' of new strikes on Iran; at least three civilians reported killed inside Iran. Iran retaliates against Jordan and Kuwait, killing a worker in Kuwait. Trump says it is now our turn to hit Iran hard.

threads.title: Federal Reserve rate path
threads.current_state: The FOMC voted 9-3 on July 29 to hold at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting; the three dissents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) all wanted a hike. Markets sold off hard: S&P -1.52% to 7,316.15, Nasdaq -1.74% to 24,442.94, 10Y up to about 4.66%, on fears the Fed is behind on inflation. Friday's August 1 jobs report is the next major test.
threads.why_it_matters: Rates are the operating system of Alex's professional world (CRE capital markets) and the macro backdrop for everything else.

timeline.summary: Hike odds rising toward 46%; BofA sees three hikes by December.
Hike odds collapse to 13.3% amid Iran-driven oil shock.
Sharp selloff on oil breaking $100; hike odds more than double to roughly 36.5%.
Monday premarket futures jump as oil craters; hike odds around 35% for Wednesday.
FOMC's two-day meeting formally opens; hike odds hold in the mid-to-high 30s.
Decision due today at 2 PM ET; hike odds climb further to about 38%; overnight Iran escalation adds a fresh input hours before the vote.
FOMC votes 9-3 to hold at 3.50-3.75 percent; Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan dissent in favor of a hike. Market reads the hold as hawkish: S&P -1.52%, Nasdaq -1.74%, 10Y up to roughly 4.66%.

threads.title: Marlins wild card race
threads.current_state: Down 6-0, Miami completed the sweep of the Phillies with an 8-6 win, its biggest comeback of the season - Conine's go-ahead pinch-hit homer plus two RBIs each from Lopez, Hernandez, and Edwards. Miami is 55-54, three straight wins, opening a four-game series at the Mets tonight, four days before the August 3 deadline. Plan: keep Alcantara, Eury Perez, Max Meyer, Joe Mack; open to trading Edwards, Lopez, Hicks, Hernandez.
threads.why_it_matters: First real playoff chase in years; the second-half schedule and trade deadline decide it.

timeline.summary: Hit the break 52-45, holding WC pole position.
10th straight loss, first time since June 2011; falls to 52-52.
Streak reaches 12, an outright franchise record; falls to 52-53.
8-7 walk-off win reported; later corrected to have occurred Monday, not Tuesday.
Correction: walk-off was Monday. Tuesday was a separate 1-0 win; Miami has won two straight, stands 54-54.
Trade deadline plan surfaces: keep Alcantara, Perez, Meyer, Mack; open to trading Edwards, Lopez, Hicks, Hernandez.
Down 6-0, Miami completes the sweep with an 8-6 comeback win, its biggest of the season; improves to 55-54, three straight wins.

threads.title: 2026 CRE capital markets under pressure
threads.current_state: South Florida commercial sales volume remains down 13% year over year; Waste Management's $379M Medley purchase was 96% seller-financed. A LoopNet analysis of roughly 5,000 listings now puts Miami's average office asking rent, $59.66/sq ft, ahead of New York's $50.56 - the highest of any US market.
threads.why_it_matters: A direct read on how tight capital markets actually are for Alex's CRE world, and how much capital migration has repriced his own market, beneath the deal-volume headlines.

threads.title: Miami Marine Stadium's restoration referendum
threads.current_state: Miami voters decide Marine Stadium's future in an August 18 referendum (Referendum #172) on a 40-year Global Spectrum/Oak View management deal. City keeps 93% of event revenue and 85% of sponsorship income, plus up to $10M toward restoration and a separate $65-85M restoration bond. Early voting runs August 3-16.
threads.why_it_matters: A civic landmark restoration decision with a real public vote and timeline.

timeline.summary: City Commission approved the management deal in February; referendum set for August 18.
Detail surfaces: Referendum #172, early voting Aug 3-16, specific revenue split, separate $65-85M restoration bond.
